exposure: in vitro fertilization and embryo transfer (IVF-ET)
cohort: The study included 20,882 advanced maternal age (>=35 years) women with singleton pregnancies (>=24 weeks) receiving care at a large tertiary maternity hospital.
finding: Advanced maternal age women undergoing IVF-ET are associated with an elevated risk of abnormal placentation, preeclampsia, gestational diabetes mellitus, and preterm birth.
mod_finding: Higher cesarean section rates were found to mediate adverse neonatal outcomes and an increased risk of postpartum hemorrhage, explaining 21.47% and 26.15% of IVF-ET's effect on postpartum hemorrhage and neonatal jaundice, respectively.
